title: Mathematics of Data Science
description: Mathematical foundations for modern data science, emphasizing probability theory and its applications in high-dimensional settings.
syllabus: Fundamentals of Probability: conditioning, independence, basic axioms
Limiting Phenomena: behavior of sequences of random variables
Concentration Inequalities: bounding tail probabilities for high-dimensional data analysis
Random Structures and their applications

title: Scientific Computing
description: An overview of scientific computing applying computational approaches to natural sciences, with an emphasis on optimization, modeling, and signal processing.
syllabus: Fundamental methods in mathematics, physics, chemistry, computer science, and biology
Optimization techniques
Modeling and signal processing applications

title: Algorithms and Data Structures
description: Fundamental principles of algorithm design and essential data structures to evaluate efficiency, design, analyze, and implement algorithms.
syllabus: Algorithm Analysis: Runtime analysis, Big-O, Omega and Theta notation
Design Paradigms: Brute force, greedy algorithms, divide-and-conquer, dynamic programming
Data Structures: Stacks, queues, linked lists, trees, heaps, hash tables, disjoint sets
Algorithms: Searching, sorting, numeric computations, string matching, graph algorithms
Complexity Theory: Polynomial reductions, P vs. NP

title: Foundations of Artificial Intelligence
description: Introduction to the basic concepts, theoretical foundations, and practical applications of classical Artificial Intelligence problems.
syllabus: Introduction and History of Artificial Intelligence
Rational Agents and environments
Problem Solving: State-space search, combinatorial optimization
Constraint Satisfaction Problems (CSPs)
Logic for knowledge representation and reasoning
Automated planning and search algorithms for board games

title: Machine Learning
description: Theoretical and practical foundations of machine learning, covering supervised, unsupervised, and advanced models.
syllabus: Probabilities, generative models, and statistical learning theory
Supervised Learning: Frequentist and Bayesian approaches, regression, classification, sparse models, SVMs, kernel methods
Neural Networks: Feed-forward, recurrent topologies, encoder-decoder models
Unsupervised Models: Mixture models, clustering, PCA, CCA, Variational autoencoders, deep information bottlenecks
prerequisites: Basic knowledge of pattern recognition, numerical analysis, and statistics

title: Foundations of Deep Learning
description: Rigorous mathematical and theoretical framework of deep neural networks, covering network behavior, optimization, and generalization.
syllabus: Linear networks, activation functions, basic architectures
Approximation Theory and Universal Approximation
Optimization techniques and landscape of neural networks
Generalization bounds and conditions
Advanced Concepts: Neural Tangent Kernels, complexity theory, regularization, adversarial robustness
prerequisites: Proficiency in Linear Algebra, Calculus, Probability Theory, and basic Topology. Familiarity with core ML concepts.

title: Modern Reinforcement Learning: From Agents to LLMs
description: Transition from traditional agent-based reinforcement learning to modern applications involving Large Language Models.
syllabus: Fundamentals of Reinforcement Learning: core theory, algorithms, decision-making
Agentic AI: Architectures for autonomous agents and multi-agent coordination
RL and LLMs: Alignment techniques (RLHF), agentic workflows, fine-tuning
Practical Implementation of agents using deep RL and LLMs

title: Generative Modeling with Diffusion Models and Stochastic Interpolants
description: Foundational mathematical toolkit for generative modeling, bridging probability theory, stochastic processes, and machine learning.
syllabus: Mathematical Foundations: Stochastic differential equations (SDEs), Fokker-Planck equation
Core Methodologies: Score-based learning, denoising objectives
Stochastic interpolants as a unifying framework
MCMC sampling and algorithms
Applications in image synthesis, scientific simulations, inverse problems
prerequisites: Comfort with calculus, linear algebra, and basic probability

title: Machine Learning on Graphs, Groups and Manifolds
description: Geometric Deep Learning covering representation learning on non-Euclidean surfaces, symmetry, and topological data analysis.
syllabus: Graphs: Representation learning, GNNs, spectral graph theory, link prediction, node classification
Groups: Symmetry and group theory, equivariance in neural networks
Manifolds: Manifold learning and dimensionality reduction
Advanced Models: Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs), Graph Attention Networks (GATs)
prerequisites: Linear algebra, multivariable calculus, probability/statistics, Python programming

title: Computer Networks
description: Advanced-level networking course exploring modern architectural shifts, data-centric networking, and Software Defined Networking.
syllabus: Beyond traditional addressing to data-centric / name-based networking
Software Defined Networking (SDN) for data centers
Push-only networking and data deltas
Decentralized system design and networked systems

title: Distributed Information Systems
description: Architectures, mechanisms, and protocols for coordinating and accessing distributed databases and information systems for data science.
syllabus: Fundamental principles and challenges of distributed information systems
Architectural paradigms in distributed environments
Mechanisms and protocols for coordinating distributed databases
Infrastructures supporting distributed applications deployment

title: High Performance Computing
description: Design, implementation, and optimization of high-performance applications on diverse parallel system architectures.
syllabus: Parallel Systems Architectures: multi-core to large-scale clusters
Programming Models: OpenMP, MPI, OpenACC, CUDA
Performance Engineering: Reproducibility, scalability, resource utilization, fault tolerance
HPC in the age of AI and big data analytics

title: Foundations of Distributed Systems
description: Basic principles of parallel and distributed systems, focusing on parallelizing large-scale problems across computing entities.
syllabus: Fundamental principles of distributed and parallel systems
Parallelization and distribution of algorithms
Coordination across multi-core and clustered environments
Preparation for advanced network and HPC coursework

title: Continuous Optimization
description: In-depth theoretical treatment of classical and modern optimization methods, convergence rates, and non-convex applications.
syllabus: Foundations of convex analysis
Gradient Descent and convergence rates
Subgradient methods and stochastic optimization
Optimality, lower bounds, and constrained optimization
Non-convex optimization
prerequisites: Analysis, linear algebra, and ability to write mathematical proofs

title: Privacy-Preserving Methods for Data Science and Distributed Systems
description: Exploration of privacy-enhancing technologies to share and analyze data without violating privacy rights.
syllabus: Private Data Sharing: Anonymization, de-anonymization, k-anonymity, differential privacy
Synthetic data generation
Private Data Analysis: Homomorphic encryption, secret sharing, SMPC
Privacy-preserving machine learning (DPSGD, PATE)
Federated learning
prerequisites: Basic data science and distributed systems knowledge
